newsitem.title: USA: Rubbermaid sees soft demand, high costs.
newsitem.headline: Rubbermaid sees soft demand, high costs.

text.p: Rubbermaid Inc said on Wednesday that increases in raw material costs, soft retail demand and lagging sales of its Little Tikes juvenile products will challenge its performance through the remainder of the year.
The company reported net earnings per share of $0.31 for the third quarter of 1996, compared with $0.32 per share in the same period last year.
It said that lower sales of outdoor juvenile products and sharp increases in resin costs had a negative effect on the quarter.
Going forward, the company said it sees developments like the recent acquisition of Graco Children's Products Inc and continued progress on globalization contributing to 1997 growth.

Rubbermaid added that its two-year realignment plan, launched last December, is on track and improvements in cost structure and customer service should translate into improved financial results in 1997 and beyond.
